node.title: Re^3: XML::LibXML::XPathContext->string_value - should ALL of the descendant's text be there?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Actually, I *do* believe that the text "World" belongs to the b element and, therefore, not to the p element.

Sure, that's up to you. I can't speak to how other modules implemented it, but I'd refer you to the [http://xmlsoft.org/|libxml2 documentation], and the [https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/|Document Object Model Specification] for all the "official" details.

Anyway, I described two ways you can get the text nodes of the current node. Using the XPath expression I showed is probably easiest. I can't really say more since you haven't described what it is you're trying to do with the document.

use warnings; use strict; use XML::LibXML; my $doc = XML::LibXML->load_xml( string => <<'EOT' ); Title_Text

paragraph_text

innnermost_text
EOT for my $node ($doc->findnodes('//*')) { print "<<<", $node->nodeName, ">>>\n"; my @texts = map { $_->data } $node->findnodes('./text()'); use Data::Dump; dd @texts; # Debug } __END__ <<>> (" \n ", " \n ", " ") <<>> (" ", " ") <<>> "Title_Text" <<<body>>> (" \n ", "\n ", " \n ") <<<p>>> "paragraph_text" <<<div>>> (" \n ", "\n ") <<<div>>> " \n innnermost_text\n " </c> <p>You could also use [mod://XML::LibXML::SAX] to get an event-based parser.</p>
